summary:
Ad Astra Ultra is an interactive 3D space mission design and simulation game developed to address NASA Space Apps Challenge’s “Space Mission Design Game” challenge. It allows players to design and configure a spacecraft, select and assemble components, prepare a mission, validate the vehicle, launch it, and monitor its flight through real-time telemetry and a final mission report.
The project makes space mission engineering more accessible by turning complex concepts—such as vehicle design, mass distribution, propulsion, staging, atmospheric flight, and scientific data collection—into an interactive experience. Players can explore how engineering choices affect mission outcomes and learn through experimentation.
Ad Astra Ultra is important because it helps make the challenges of space exploration understandable and engaging. By combining 3D visualization, mission simulation, and bilingual support in English and Italian, it offers an educational way to discover the decisions and trade-offs involved in designing a space mission.
details:
Project Details – Ad Astra Ultra

Ad Astra Ultra is a browser-based 3D space mission design and simulation game. It guides players through the main stages of a space mission, from spacecraft construction and mission configuration to launch, flight monitoring, and mission evaluation.

Players interact with a 3D editor to assemble a vehicle using different components, configure its characteristics, and check whether it meets the mission’s launch requirements. Once launched, the simulation displays flight telemetry, including altitude, flight time, and scientific data received. At the end of the mission, a report presents the outcome and evaluates the mission’s performance.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming aspects of space mission engineering into an accessible, hands-on learning experience. Instead of simply reading about spacecraft design, players can experiment with different configurations and observe how engineering decisions influence the outcome. The atmospheric probe demonstration provides a complete example of a mission, including parachute deployment and scientific data collection.

The intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space exploration, promote STEM learning, and make the complexity of mission design easier to understand. The game supports both English and Italian, helping it reach a broader audience.

Ad Astra Ultra was developed using JavaScript and HTML, with Three.js (WebGL) for 3D graphics. The project uses a browser-based architecture and does not require a dedicated installation. Development and testing also involved TypeScript, automated testing tools, and Playwright for browser-based end-to-end verification.

Its creative approach combines interactive spacecraft construction, real-time 3D visualization, flight simulation, and mission scoring in a single educational experience. Key factors considered during development included usability, accessibility, engineering constraints, vehicle configuration, propulsion, mass distribution, atmospheric flight, telemetry, and the clarity of feedback provided to players.
